requirement_text.REQ-063: Execute Decision 0006's D1: relocate users, groups and tenant_role from the public schema into each tenant's own Postgres schema via :prefix. Full design: lib/letflow/design/req063-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md. Full decision record and security rationale: docs/migration/decisions/0006-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md, section 3 especially -- that section is THE reason this run has a HIGH-priority security gate: moving users per-schema changes the meaning of two shipped unique indexes (username; external_realm+external_id), and decision 0006 section 3.2's central claim (the global one-OIDC-identity-per-user guarantee relocates from users to tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index rather than being lost) is explicitly flagged in the decision record itself as needing independent SECURITY-REVIEWER re-derivation, not acceptance on the decision's own say-so.

task.description:
Read context.artifacts_in and git diff main...HEAD on this branch. This diff touches a tenant-data path -- scope test result is YES, in scope, do not skip to out-of-scope PASS.

Run the full INV-1..INV-8 checklist per security-invariants.md, but weight your time toward these four items this run's own history makes highest-risk, each with a specific claim to verify rather than accept:

1. **INV-1 (tenant isolation) -- decision 0006 section 3.2's central claim.** The users migration's unique_index(:users, [:username]) and the external-identity partial index both become per-tenant-schema-scoped rather than global once users moves off the public schema. Decision 0006 argues the global one-OIDC-identity-per-user guarantee is RELOCATED to tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index (a realm binds to exactly one tenant, immutably) rather than lost. Independently re-derive this yourself against the actual shipped migrations -- read priv/repo/migrations/20260816000001_create_tenants.exs's tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index directly, and lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex's update_changeset/2 to confirm idp_realm_id truly cannot be reassigned after creation. Do not accept decision 0006's argument on its own say-so -- this is the one thing this whole run exists to have you check.

2. **INV-7 (SQL injication / identifier safety) -- the drop migration's dynamic EXECUTE format(...).** priv/repo/migrations/20260819000004_drop_legacy_public_identity_tables.exs reads schema_name values out of public.tenant_schemas and interpolates them into a dynamic EXECUTE format(...) statement to build its per-row existence check across N tenant schemas (schema_name isn't known at migration-write time, only at migration-run time). The migration's own header comment argues schema_name is safe because it only ever holds values Letflow.TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 produced (tenant_[0-9a-f]{32} shape, constrained by Ecto.UUID.cast/1, never free text) and is read back from a column this project's own code populated, never accepted as a migration parameter. Verify this claim directly: confirm no code path lets an arbitrary string land in tenant_schemas.schema_name (check the column's origin at every INSERT into that table, not just the one you'd expect), and confirm the migration's EXECUTE format(...) uses %I (identifier quoting) or an equivalent safe-quoting mechanism for schema_name and %L/parameterization for any literal values, not raw string concatenation.

3. **INV-1/INV-8 -- the drop migration's guard mechanism (ELIXIR-DEV's own engineering call, explicitly flagged for you).** Design section 5 left the guard mechanism as an open question; ELIXIR-DEV implemented a per-row existence check (by primary key) rather than a row-count-parity check or an operator flag, with reasoning recorded in the migration's own header comment and in handoffs/WF02-REQ063-20260818/step-02a-elixir-dev.json's result.summary/issues. Evaluate this call on its merits: does a per-row PK-existence check actually close the corruption gap it claims to (a row landing in the wrong tenant while another goes missing, with counts still balancing)? Is skip-all-three-tables-on-any-single-missing-row the right failure mode, or does it risk never being able to complete the cutover if even one tenant is perpetually out of sync? State your own verdict, don't just confirm ELIXIR-DEV's reasoning is internally consistent.

4. **INV-8 (unresolved {:ok,_} matches on external-I/O paths) -- provision_oidc_user/3 to /4's arity change.** Confirm lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex's updated call site correctly handles a new possible error case (if TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 fails) rather than assuming success, and that no other caller of the old /3 arity was missed (grep for provision_oidc_user across the whole lib/ and test/ tree, not just the design doc's claimed single caller).

For every other INV-2..INV-6 not named above, run your standard APPLIES/NOT-APPLICABLE determination and check as usual -- don't skip them, just don't over-invest relative to the four above.
acceptance_criteria: Verdict stated per invariant, INV-1 through INV-8, APPLIES or NOT-APPLICABLE, with a PASS/FAIL for each APPLIES invariant

INV-1's decision-0006-section-3.2 claim independently re-derived against the actual shipped tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index and Tenant.update_changeset/2, not accepted from the decision record's own text
INV-7's dynamic EXECUTE format(...) verified for identifier-quoting safety, not just trusted from the migration's own header comment
ELIXIR-DEV's guard-mechanism engineering call evaluated on its own merits with an independent verdict, not merely confirmed as internally consistent
provision_oidc_user's arity change confirmed to have no missed callers and correct new-error-case handling
FAIL immediately, no partial credit, if any APPLIES invariant fails

result.summary:
Scope test: YES, in scope (three new tenant-scoped identity migrations, one drop migration with dynamic EXECUTE format(...), tenant_provisioning.ex/identity.ex/auth_pipeline.ex changes). Ran git diff main...HEAD (19 files, +1808/-35) and read every artifact in artifacts_in directly, not the design doc's own claims.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. (a) prefix-scoping: read priv/repo/migrations/20260819000001/2/3_..._tenant_scoped.exs directly -- each wraps its create table/create index calls in `if prefix() do ... end` with `prefix: prefix()` passed to every table/index call (mandatory guard pattern, confirmed present in all three files, e.g. users migration lines 60-84). (b) manifest registration: read lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex's @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest directly (lines 286-291) -- all three create migrations are registered in FK-correct order (groups, tenant_role, users); confirmed 20260819000004 (the drop) is correctly ABSENT from this manifest (it is a global-schema, run-once migration per its own header comment, not tenant-replayed -- verified this is the right call, not an omission). (c) tenant_id derivation: Group/User schemas retain a plain `field(:tenant_id, Ecto.UUID)` (grep-confirmed, lib/letflow/identity/user.ex, group.ex) -- tenant_id is caller-resolved and passed as an already-authoritative argument, matching this codebase's pre-existing (unchanged by this diff) discipline per 0003's addendum; Letflow.Identity.provision_oidc_user/4's own @doc states tenant_id is 'trusted as already-resolved/authoritative by the caller,' never identity_context.tenant_id (the token-claimed hint) -- read lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex's provision_user/3 and confirmed it passes the step-2 DB-resolved tenant.id, not any client-suppliable value. This is pre-existing project convention, not a regression.

**INV-1 item 1 (Decision 0006 section 3.2's central claim) -- independently re-derived, CONFIRMED, not accepted on the decision record's own say-so.** Read priv/repo/migrations/20260816000001_create_tenants.exs directly: `create unique_index(:tenants, [:idp_realm_id], where: "idp_realm_id IS NOT NULL", name: :tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index)` -- a real, DB-enforced partial unique index on tenants.idp_realm_id, unconditional on tenant status. Read lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex's update_changeset/2 directly: `cast(attrs, [:display_name, :status])` -- idp_realm_id (and slug) are structurally absent from the castable field list, so no value from any caller-supplied attrs map can ever reach idp_realm_id through this changeset; there is no separate admin/rotation changeset function in the module (grep-confirmed only create_changeset/3 and update_changeset/2 exist). Grepped the whole lib/ tree for other write paths to idp_realm_id or Tenant records (Repo.update_all, raw changeset construction) -- none exist; the only read is Identity.resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 (Repo.get_by, read-only). Verdict: decision 0006 section 3.2's claim holds up against the actual shipped code -- the global one-OIDC-identity-per-user guarantee genuinely relocates to tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index (one realm binds to exactly one tenant, immutably, DB- and changeset-enforced) rather than being lost when users' external-identity uniqueness became per-tenant-schema-scoped.

**INV-1 item 3 / guard mechanism -- independent verdict, not merely confirmed as internally consistent.** Read priv/repo/migrations/20260819000004_drop_legacy_public_identity_tables.exs's full DO $$ block. The per-row PK-existence check (NOT EXISTS by id, per tenant schema) genuinely closes the specific gap row-count parity cannot: a row misrouted to the wrong tenant schema while another goes missing will show as a miss under the existence check (id absent from its OWNING tenant's schema) even if global counts still balance -- correct reasoning, verified against the actual SQL, not just the comment. One narrower gap noted, non-blocking: the check verifies id-presence only, not content -- a row that landed with a stale/mismatched payload under a correct id in the correct schema (only reachable via a bug in copy_tenant/2's own tenant_id-filtered SELECT, which is correctly scoped) would pass the guard undetected. This does not create a cross-tenant leak (INV-1's actual concern) and is not realistically reachable given copy_tenant/2's query shape, so it is a defense-in-depth observation, not a BLOCKER -- filing as a MINOR note, not blocking this gate. On the availability question: skip-all-three-tables-on-any-single-miss is the correct failure mode for a data-loss-prevention gate, not a security defect -- the legacy public tables remain fully readable/writable while the drop is pending (the migration only ever removes, never blocks, live traffic), a stuck tenant blocks only the LEGACY-TABLE CLEANUP step, and ELIXIR-DEV's own verification empirically exercised both the skip path and the recovery path (insert uncopied row -> guard skips -> run mix letflow.copy_identity_tables -> re-migrate -> guard proceeds) against real Postgres. My independent verdict: this is the right tradeoff -- zero risk of an irreversible drop with unrecovered tenant data, in exchange for a fully-recoverable stall, not a permanent block.

INV-2, INV-3, INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE (no multi-tenant API response surface, no scripting/plugin runtime, no lookup-by-ID endpoint exists yet; S4/S5 not started, consistent with security-invariants.md's own applicability note).

INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- APPLIES, PASS. Ran both required greps scoped to this diff's own files (identity.ex, identity_migration.ex, letflow.copy_identity_tables.ex, auth_pipeline.ex, tenant_provisioning.ex, the four new migrations): zero hits on the hardcoded-secret heuristic. No secret material is threaded through any handoff file, log call, or return value in this diff.

**INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) -- APPLIES, PASS, independently verified against the actual SQL text, not the migration's own header-comment claim.** Read the drop migration's EXECUTE format(...) calls directly (three of them, for groups/users/tenant_role): each uses `%I` for the identifier position (v_tenant.schema_name, the dynamic per-tenant schema) and `%L` for the literal position (v_tenant.tenant_id) -- confirmed correct positional usage (%I quotes as a double-quoted identifier, %L quotes/escapes as a literal), not raw string concatenation or bare interpolation anywhere in the block. Traced every INSERT into public.tenant_schemas (grep for 'tenant_schemas' and 'Repo.insert'/'%Registration{' across lib/ and priv/repo/migrations/): exactly one write path exists, Letflow.TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 -> insert_or_fetch_registration/2 -> Repo.insert(Registration.changeset(...)) (tenant_provisioning.ex line ~385). Registration.changeset/2 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/registration.ex) independently enforces `validate_format(:schema_name, ~r/^tenant_[0-9a-f]{32}$/)` on every write as defense-in-depth (added per ISS-0027/GH#85, not just call-graph discipline) -- so even a hypothetical future second writer could not insert a schema_name outside the tenant_[0-9a-f]{32} shape without failing this changeset validation first. schema_name itself is derived only via schema_name_for_tenant/1, which only proceeds past Ecto.UUID.cast/1 (rejects anything not a valid UUID). No other Repo.query/Repo.query! hit anywhere in lib/ or priv/repo/migrations/ interpolates tenant/user-controlled data (the only other hits -- sandbox_pool.ex, sandbox_pool/fixture_loader.ex -- are pre-existing, out of this diff's scope, and use the same schema_name-from-trusted-derivation pattern). Verdict: the identifier-safety claim in the migration's own header comment is TRUE, confirmed against the SQL text and the full write-path trace, not accepted on the comment's word.

**INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES, PASS.** provision_oidc_user/3 -> /4 arity change: grepped the entire lib/ tree for provision_oidc_user -- exactly one runtime call site exists, lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex line 178 (Identity.provision_oidc_user(identity_context, tenant_id, jit_config, prefix: schema_name)); all other hits are moduledoc/comment references or test files. Read auth_pipeline.ex's provision_user/3 directly: it does NOT assume TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 succeeds -- it `case`s on the result, handling both {:ok, schema_name} (proceeds to call provision_oidc_user/4) and {:error, :invalid_tenant_id} (maps to {:error, {:provision, :invalid_tenant_id}}, which falls through call/2's existing {:error, {:provision, _reason}} catch-all to a 500 response) -- no bare {:ok, _} = match anywhere in this chain. Ran `grep -rn "^\s*{:ok, .*} = " lib/letflow/` project-wide: every hit is inside a case clause pattern, not a bare crashing match. Note (disclosed by ELIXIR-DEV in step-02a, independently confirmed, not a new finding): test/letflow/identity_test.exs and test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs still call the old 3-arity signature (15+ call sites) and will fail to compile/run against provision_oidc_user/4 -- this is explicitly test-fixture staleness the design doc's own §7 item 4 predicted and deferred to TEST-DESIGNER's Step 3, not a production code defect and not an INV-8 violation (the production call site itself is correct); flagging here only to confirm I verified it's the disclosed, scoped case and not a missed caller.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) -- APPLIES, PASS by virtue of this handoff itself existing with an explicit per-invariant breakdown.

No APPLIES invariant failed. One MINOR non-blocking observation filed (INV-1 item 3's content-match gap, defense-in-depth only, not realistically reachable) -- not a BLOCKER, does not gate this PASS.

issues.description: priv/repo/migrations/20260819000004_drop_legacy_public_identity_tables.exs's per-row guard check verifies row PRESENCE (by id) in the destination tenant schema, not row CONTENT. A row that exists under the correct id in the correct tenant schema but with stale/mismatched data (only reachable via a defect in copy_tenant/2's own tenant_id-filtered SELECT, which is correctly scoped today) would pass the guard undetected. Not a cross-tenant leak and not realistically reachable given the current copy_tenant/2 implementation -- defense-in-depth note only, does not block this PASS. No action required unless copy_tenant/2's selection logic changes in a future requirement.
